title: From plasma membrane to cytosol: how NPH3 phase separation shapes phototropism
content: Plants bend toward light with remarkable precision, translating subtle environmental cues into directional growth. This elegant response is known as phototropism. The process depends on the blue light-mediated activation of phototropins (phot1 and phot2) at the plasma membrane and the subsequent formation of a lateral auxin gradient. Although the early phototropic signaling component NON-PHOTOTROPIC HYPOCOTYL 3 (NPH3) has emerged as a central hub linking blue light perception to auxin distribution (Reuter et al. 2021; Sullivan et al. 2021), its molecular mode of action has remained unclear.
